item.title: Transition Your Wardrobe Sewing Workshop — Sun Aug 16, 5:00 PM — Lovlee Art Studios
item.description:
Join us and learn basic sewing and design techniques to update your wardrobe to match your gender identity and style! Learning to sew is a great life skill to have, you can make your own repairs and adjustments, as well as repurpose old clothes to turn them into one of a kind fashion. No sewing experience necessary. Bring one piece of clothing you would like to upcycle. If you have a sewing machine or sewing needles and materials from home you want to use you are welcome to bring in and use during this session. We will have some sewing materials and tools on hand for you to use and get creative. Allies are also welcome to join. This event is in partnership with Out Montclair. item.title: NJBS Blues & Brews: Marcela de Campos live at Montclair Brewery — Sun Aug 16, 5:30 PM — Montclair Brewery
item.description: Join us for the next installment of our monthly collab with the North Jersey Blues Society known as Blues + Brews. One Sunday a month, we collaborate to bring the Blues to Montclair. Next up – Marcela de Campos! Marcela de Campos is a Blues Rock guitarist known for her fiery tone, expressive phrasing and electrifying live performances. Rooted in the tradition of Albert King, B.B. King and Eric Clapton, her playing blends traditional blues with modern rock. Marcela released her debut EP featuring Scott Henderson and her latest album Dimmed Lights (2024), captures her gritty tone and high energy style. She has collaborated with artists including Guthrie Govan, and Philip Bynoe (Steve Vai), and has performed at venues such as Sony Hall, Brooklyn Bowl, The Cutting Room and Bowery Ballroom. Marcela has opened for George Porter Jr., Sons of Cream, Ana Popovic and was featured twice in the 2025-26 season performing during the New York Knicks Halftime show at Madison Square Garden. $10 cover

item.title: Going Global: A Free Two-Part Workshop Series — Tue Aug 18, 12:00 PM — Online
item.description:
Ready to take your business beyond U.S. borders? Join us for a FREE two-part workshop series designed to transform your growth from local to worldwide. On August 4, we'll explore whether exporting is the right move for your business, assess your readiness, and identify which of your products or services have international demand. By August 18, you'll be ready for part two, where we'll dive into the real logistics—finding international buyers, navigating permits and paperwork, and mapping out your clear path forward. Expert facilitator Reina Valenzuela will guide you through the opportunities, close your knowledge gaps, and leave you with a concrete action plan. Whether you're curious about global expansion or ready to take the leap, this free series gives you the framework and clarity to do it right.
Hosted by: Feliciano Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation

item.title: Montclair Mixtape: Build-a-Zine with WMSC — Wed Aug 19, 3:00 PM — University Hall Room 2044
item.description: What if you could bottle up the very beginning of your Montclair story? Montclair Mixtape is a collaborative Welcome Week zine where every student gets to create a page that captures who they are right now—their favorite songs, big goals, random interests, and everything they hope to experience during their first year at Montclair. Then, make it yours! Decorate your page with stickers, doodles, magazine cutouts, colors, lyrics, photos, or anything else that feels like you. While creating, students can chat, swap recommendations, discover shared interests, and get to know the people around them. Throughout Welcome Week, pages will be collected and brought together into one giant collaborative “Montclair Mixtape” zine—a snapshot of the students, dreams, personalities, and playlists that make up YOUR first week on campus. item.title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes) — Wed Aug 26, 11:00 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.
There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.
Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.
Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.
The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.
Source: Meetup: The Mindful Stream
